title: 01 Your original
note: Your untouched 320x179 drawing. Keep a duplicate before experimenting.

title: 02 Group values
note: Reduce the ground to broad shapes, mute the purple grass strip, and separate cool distant trees from warm near trunks. Texture can wait.

title: 03 Build distant depth
note: Place faint, overlapping tree shapes behind the existing foreground trunks. Work on a background layer; keep the near silhouettes visible.

title: 04 Rebuild large shapes
note: Repaint larger tapering trunks and asymmetric branches. Block foliage as masses. This is the largest composition change: a reference study, not a hidden automatic cleanup.

title: 05 Refine distant trees
note: Add variation to far tree edges. Their small value differences should stay quieter than foreground shapes. Avoid outlining every distant tree.

title: 06 Shade trunks and ground
note: Use broad shadow planes and a few broken vertical bark marks. Give the forest floor a continuous base instead of repeating bright plants everywhere.

title: 07 Shade foliage masses
note: Shade leaf masses with dark interiors and small lit clusters. Place clusters around branch tips, varying their density and leaving irregular gaps.

title: 08 Restrained highlights
note: Use sparse olive highlights on leaf tops, herbs, and the ground edge. The final frame is the supplied reference resized, mapped to the game palette, and simplified to reduce isolated texture pixels.
